We differentiate the given function with respect to $x,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the chain rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(y-{x}^{2})) \\  & =\frac{1}{y-{x}^{2}}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(y-{x}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we use the sum and constant multiple rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{y-{x}^{2}}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(y-{x}^{2}) & =\frac{1}{y-{x}^{2}}\cdot (y\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(1)-\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2})) \\  & =\frac{1}{y-{x}^{2}}\cdot (y\cdot 0-2x) \\  & =-\frac{2x}{y-{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(1,9)\mathbin{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(1,9) & =-\frac{2\cdot 1}{9-{1}^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{2}{8} \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
